items.text: Pre-diagnostic risk associations in cancer-free populations differ from prognosis in those with cancer, and the distinct roles of membrane-bound versus soluble proteins constitute a specific question.
Repeated measures of six proteins and lifestyle/genetic determinants can provide insights into temporal trajectories and sources of variation, not merely a cross-sectional correlation.
Leveraging existing ARIC multi-omics and follow-up for an R03 preliminary association study has reusable discovery value even if it cannot confirm mechanisms or immediately improve screening.

SOMAscan reproducibility does not equal specificity for target proteins/soluble forms; RFU, genetic variant effects on binding, and shared factor heterogeneity limit biological interpretation, with orthogonal validation to follow.

Follow-up start has been reset to Visit 3/5 with a 2/5-year lag; reverse causality, time-varying confounding, long-term survival/selection, and precision with only 56 post-Visit 5 events must still be addressed, though it cannot be said that temporal protection is entirely absent.

MR is a secondary exploration; selecting instruments based on protein and CRC concurrent associations, MHC linkage/pleiotropy, and binding artifacts mean F>10 is insufficient to establish causality, and this cannot be used to negate the independent observational objective.
